newsitem.title: UK: Nervous short sterling may rally despite rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Nervous short sterling may rally despite rate rise.

text.p: British short sterling futures are expected to be volatile after the surprise rate quarter point rate rise on Wednesday, but analysts said there is scope for all but the front month contracts to rally.

The Bank of England raised the minimum lending rate to 6.0 percent from 5.75 percent after the monthly monetary meeting between Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
"There will still be nervousness about another rate hike ahead of the election," said Philip Shaw, at Union Discount.

"On balance short sterling will continue to discount another 25 basis point hike in rates because the market will be nervous that the economy will continue to grow strongly," said chief economist Shaw.
"But having had the initial fall we should see some recovery in the short sterling strip although certainly not the sorts of levels seen before the news at mid-day," he said.
March short sterling initially fell on the move and at 1302 GMT was trading at 93.60 down 16 basis points on the day, discounting another quarter point rate rise by the end of the first quarter.
December short sterling was at 93.76, down 0.16 on the day.

"We pushed down agressively in the front four or five contracts," said a trader at Cater Allen. "The front three could stage a minor recovery. December could go back up as high as 93.84 and March back to 93.66."
He said the markets would view Clarke's actions as prudent stewardship of the economy.

"For short sterling the interesting thing will be whether this is a one off and rates will stay where they are until the election, or whether Clarke's hand been triggered by expectations that growth is building up," the trader said.

"If we see data that confirm (the strengthening of the economy) then the back months will come under more pressure and back months spread will widen out as the market looks for more hikes down the road," he said.
Adam Cole, UK economist at HSBC James Capel, said the front month contracts were good value at the moment.

"Short sterling is pricing another quarter point off three- month money by end of this year and a quarter point more by March of next year," he said. "By moving relatively early on base rates the Chancellor is trying to avoid having to raise again this side of the election...he can probably do that."
